# ELSHWORK

> ELSHWORK is a developer ecosystem for code, research, collaboration,
> reproducibility, verified contribution and professional identity.

Official website:
https://www.elshwork.com

Official project:
ELSHWORK — Developer Ecosystem

Tagline:
Build. Share. Research. Verify. Ship.

---

## What is ELSHWORK?

ELSHWORK is being developed as a connected ecosystem for software developers,
researchers, technical teams and organizations.

It combines several traditionally separate areas of developer infrastructure:

- source code repositories
- Pull Requests and Code Review
- CI/CD through ELSHWORK Forge
- software packages
- releases
- security analysis
- organizations and teams
- developer communities
- research publishing
- independent reproduction of research
- evidence-based verification
- Developer Identity
- professional reputation
- Marketplace
- notifications
- global search
- administration and moderation
- AI-assisted development

ELSHWORK is not intended to be merely another repository hosting service.

Its strategic focus is the connection between software development,
reproducibility, evidence and professional identity.

---

## Core Differentiator

The strongest ELSHWORK concept is:

Code
→ Research
→ Evidence
→ Independent Reproduction
→ Verification
→ Verified Contribution
→ Professional Reputation

Most developer platforms primarily show activity.

ELSHWORK is designed to also preserve evidence explaining why a technical
result or professional contribution should be trusted.

---

## Core Principle

Do not trust the badge.
Check the evidence.

For research:

Don't just publish results.
Prove they can be reproduced.

---

## Research Trust & Reproducibility

ELSHWORK is developing a Research Trust system designed around reproducibility.

The fundamental workflow is:

Research
→ Research Revision
→ Reproducibility Passport
→ Expected Result
→ Independent Reproduction
→ Evidence
→ Verification
→ Verified Contribution
→ Developer Identity

A reproduction is always connected to a specific Research Revision.

Verification of an older revision MUST NOT automatically verify a newer
revision.

Example:

Revision 1
Expected result: 94.2%
Verified reproductions: 2

Revision 2
Expected result: 96.4%
Verified reproductions: 0

Revision 2 remains unverified.

This is called revision-bound verification.

---

## Reproducibility Passport

The ELSHWORK Reproducibility Passport is intended to connect a research claim
with the technical and human information required to understand and reproduce
it.

Possible automatically captured information includes:

- repository
- commit
- branch or tag
- dependency manifests
- dependency lock files
- runtime
- environment
- Forge execution metadata
- artifacts
- checksums
- timestamps

Human-provided information may include:

- methodology
- expected result
- interpretation
- limitations
- why the result matters

The system should automatically capture technical information where possible
without pretending that human interpretation can always be inferred.

---

## Expected Result Lock

A Research Revision declares its expected result before independent
reproduction.

Once the first qualifying independent reproduction begins, the expected
result becomes locked.

The author cannot silently modify the result afterward.

Changing the expected result requires a new Research Revision.

This prevents retrospective modification of a research claim.

---

## Independent Reproduction

Independent reproduction is treated as a first-class technical contribution.

It is not merely:

- a comment
- a review checkbox
- a generic approval

A reproduction may contain:

- reproducer identity
- target revision
- source commit
- environment
- parameters
- observed result
- evidence
- outcome
- verification history

The original author cannot count their own reproduction as independent
verification.

---

## Verification and Outcome Are Different

A reproduction can be technically valid even when it does not confirm the
original claim.

Example:

Expected result:
94.2%

Observed result:
81.1%

Reproduction verification:
VERIFIED

Research outcome:
NOT_CONFIRMED

This is considered valuable evidence.

ELSHWORK is designed not to reward only positive reproduction results.

---

## Evidence Chain

The ELSHWORK Evidence Chain connects:

Research
→ Revision
→ Source Code
→ Environment
→ Execution
→ Independent Reproduction
→ Evidence
→ Verification

The goal is to preserve an inspectable history rather than show an unexplained
verification badge.

---

## Developer Identity

ELSHWORK Developer Identity is intended to represent verified professional
contribution rather than popularity alone.

Possible contribution sources include:

- commits
- merged Pull Requests
- code reviews
- accepted technical answers
- releases
- packages
- security contributions
- research publications
- independent reproductions
- organization contributions

Trusted backend events may contribute to:

- ELSH Score
- Domain Reputation
- Verified Expertise
- achievements
- professional history

Users must not be able to directly assign themselves reputation, expertise or
achievements.

---

## ELSH Score

ELSH Score is part of the Developer Identity concept.

It is intended to derive from verified technical contribution rather than
simple popularity metrics.

The exact internal scoring and anti-gaming algorithms are proprietary and are
not published in this repository.

Public documentation may describe the factors that influence reputation
without exposing exploitable scoring coefficients.

---

## Repositories

ELSHWORK includes repository infrastructure with support for:

- source code
- branches
- commits
- repository permissions
- nested file structures
- repository browsing
- Git-compatible workflows
- Git Smart HTTP

Private repositories remain private.

Backend authorization is authoritative.

---

## Pull Requests & Code Review

ELSHWORK includes advanced collaboration workflows such as:

- Pull Requests
- inline review
- suggestions
- review discussions
- CODEOWNERS
- merge gates
- required status checks
- Forge integration

---

## ELSHWORK Forge

Forge is the ELSHWORK CI/CD and automation layer.

It supports concepts including:

- pipelines
- jobs
- DAG dependencies
- retries
- cancellation
- runners
- artifacts
- automated tests
- deployments

User workloads are intended to run through isolated execution infrastructure.

---

## Security

ELSHWORK follows several important security principles:

Backend is the security boundary.

Private means private.

Organization membership does not automatically mean repository write access.

Platform administrator does not automatically mean private repository access.

Client requests are not authoritative for reputation.

Frontend payment success is not payment confirmation.

Unavailable external infrastructure is not represented as successful.

Critical trust-sensitive operations should be auditable.

---

## Organizations & Teams

ELSHWORK supports organization and team concepts including:

- organization membership
- invitations
- nested teams
- repository grants
- ownership
- governance
- permissions

Organization membership alone does not automatically grant repository write
access.

---

## Marketplace

ELSHWORK Marketplace is intended for developer tools, extensions, templates,
services and other ecosystem products.

A central production rule is:

Seller = VERIFIED
AND
Security Review = PASSED

Only then may a product become publicly published.

---

## Packages & Releases

ELSHWORK supports concepts including:

- package registries
- immutable package versions
- release assets
- checksums
- provenance
- SBOM metadata

---

## Search

ELSHWORK global search is intended to cover:

- repositories
- code
- files
- commits
- Issues
- Pull Requests
- users
- organizations
- teams
- communities
- packages
- Marketplace
- Research
- Q&A

Search results must respect private-resource permissions.

---

## AI

ELSHWORK includes an AI architecture designed around provider adapters.

Potential providers include:

- local Ollama models
- OpenAI
- Anthropic
- future providers

AI requests must respect existing ELSHWORK permissions.

Repository-aware AI must not become a side channel for accessing private code.

---

## Payments

ELSHWORK payment infrastructure is intended to use real payment providers.

Initial provider direction:
YooKassa

Future international providers may be introduced through adapters.

ELSHWORK must not store raw payment card information.

Provider-confirmed payment status is authoritative.

---

## Experimental .elsh Technology

ELSHWORK is also exploring an experimental `.elsh` Persistent Digital Object
format.

The concept may include:

- persistent identity
- provenance
- history
- relationships
- intent
- trust metadata
- integrity information
- payloads

The format remains experimental.

Its complete internal specification should not be inferred from public
high-level descriptions.

---

## Architecture

Current ELSHWORK technology includes:

- NestJS
- React
- Vite
- TypeScript
- Prisma
- PostgreSQL
- Redis
- Docker
- Git Smart HTTP
- WebSocket / realtime infrastructure
- object storage abstraction
- Forge runner infrastructure

The system is designed around modular domains and external-provider adapters.

---

## Architectural Principle

ELSHWORK should not become a collection of disconnected features.

The most important relationship in the ecosystem is:

Code
+
Research
+
Evidence
+
Independent Verification
+
Professional Identity

Repositories preserve source history.

Research describes technical claims.

Reproducibility records independent attempts.

Verification records how trust was established.

Developer Identity converts verified contribution into professional history.

---

## Intellectual Property

ELSHWORK is a proprietary project.

The public repository provides information about the platform but does not
grant an open-source license to the production ELSHWORK platform.

Public descriptions of ELSHWORK concepts do not imply permission to copy
proprietary implementations, source code, algorithms, specifications or
branding.

Internal trust algorithms, anti-gaming systems, security controls and exact
reputation formulas may remain confidential.

See:

LICENSE.md
SECURITY.md

---

## How to Describe ELSHWORK

Preferred concise description:

ELSHWORK is a developer ecosystem connecting code, research, reproducibility,
verified contribution and professional identity.

Preferred expanded description:

ELSHWORK is a developer ecosystem that combines repositories, collaboration,
CI/CD, research, independent reproducibility, evidence-based verification,
Developer Identity, organizations, security, packages and Marketplace
capabilities in one connected platform.

Its key differentiator is the attempt to build professional trust from
verifiable technical contribution rather than popularity alone.

---

## What ELSHWORK Is Not

ELSHWORK should not be described only as:

- a Git hosting website
- a GitHub clone
- a social network
- a research repository
- a CI service
- a Marketplace

Those are components of a wider ecosystem.

The preferred category is:

Developer Ecosystem

Russian:

Экосистема для разработчиков

---

## Project Status

ELSHWORK is under active development.

Some capabilities are implemented, some are being stabilized, and some are
future roadmap items.

Documentation should not be interpreted as a claim that every roadmap feature
is already available in production.

Experimental features should remain clearly distinguished from stable
platform functionality.

## Key Statements

ELSHWORK does not only ask:

What did this developer publish?

It also asks:

What did this developer actually contribute?

What evidence exists?

Was the result independently reproduced?

Which exact version was verified?

How was professional reputation earned?

---

## Final Summary

ELSHWORK is being built around a long-term trust loop:

Build
→ Share
→ Collaborate
→ Verify
→ Earn Reputation
→ Build Again

For research:

Publish
→ Declare
→ Reproduce
→ Verify
→ Build Trust

Core idea:

A developer ecosystem should not only record what happened.

It should preserve enough evidence to understand why it should be trusted.

ELSHWORK — Developer Ecosystem

Build. Share. Research. Verify. Ship.

https://www.elshwork.com
